Quick initial triage (logs and metrics attached):
- Confirmed: p95/p99 spike begins 2026-09-18T08:48:00Z (08:48 UTC) across 3 host pools serving NovaRetail.
- Error type: increased 504/502 responses correlated with request latency and backend cache misses.
- Throughput: RPS steady; CPU/GPU utilization normal.
- Key observation: a spike in prefix/KV cache miss rate at the same time window. Miss rate jumped from ~1.2% to ~67% (see attached logs).
- Recent change: there was a config rollout at 08:40Z that tightened cache eviction thresholds (sweeper aggressive sweep interval reduced). We pushed that change to a fraction of hosts earlier this week and rolled it further yesterday morning.

Likely hypothesis: the rollout triggered a large-scale prefix eviction wave (cold prefixes) which caused a burst of KV fetches for warmup on the model serving path. That increased tail latency and, under certain concurrent request sizes, led to transient 5xx errors as backends timed out waiting for remote KV reads.

Short-term mitigations we can enact now (recommended order):
1) Revert the eviction-threshold change for the NovaRetail route (rollback to previous TTL) — reduces eviction wave.
2) Temporarily bump KV fetch concurrency timeouts and extend backend read timeouts by +500ms to avoid cascading 502/504s.
3) Enable prefix warmup for hot routes (best-effort) while we stabilize.
4) If needed, shift NovaRetail to a dedicated pool for 1–2 hours (Marcus/Grace to confirm acceptance).

I attached: kv_prefix_eviction_log_20260918.tar.gz (sparsed logs + miss-rate timeseries) and a cropped p95_timeseries image.

Will start a rollback if we get a green light from Stephanie or product leadership.

—Dylan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the signal, Dylan — good initial analysis. A few follow-ups and plan for next steps:
1) Root cause hypothesis matches our local reproduction: the eviction sweep reduction inadvertently caused synchronized TTL expirations across multiple hosts because of how we shard prefix metadata. In short, a coordinated roll made many hosts delete the same prefix windows simultaneously.
2) Short-term plan (we can do in the next 30–45 mins):
   - Emergency rollback of the sweep interval change for the NovaRetail route (automated rollback script ready).
   - Increase the per-request KV fetch timeout and add a lightweight in-process cache (fast-path) for the next 2 hours while cold prefixes refill.
3) Medium-term fixes:
   - Staggered rollout with randomized jitter for any eviction policy changes.
   - Safe-guard: if miss-rate > 10% in a 5min window, auto-disable aggressive eviction and switch to passive warming.
   - Instrumentation: add a dedicated metric for prefix-eviction waves and a dashboard alert.

I will start the rollback after confirmation from Stephanie or product leadership. If approved, expect stabilization within ~12–25 minutes post-rollback (based on warmup characteristics).

Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Internal summary & exec ask — NovaRetail p95/p99 spike (cache invalidation wave)

Team —
Summary: NovaRetail experienced a sudden latency and error spike on 2026-09-18 caused by a prefix/KV cache invalidation wave after a recent eviction-policy rollout. Dylan/Jonas confirmed miss-rate surge and correlated logs. We rolled back the aggressive eviction config for the NovaRetail route at ~11:20 PDT and saw p95 return to ~480ms within ~18 minutes; p99 normalized over ~40 minutes.

Customer impact: checkout flows degraded for ~40 minutes; error rate peaked ~5%. NovaRetail requires a formal post-mortem and wants assurance this won't recur. Marcus will own customer comms and credit proposal; Grace to prepare PSR/post-mortem.

Action items / Exec asks:
- Leadership approval to make the rollback permanent for the NovaRetail route until the staggered-rollout guard and metrics are in place (Jonas estimate: 2 sprint work to harden; we can fast-track the guard in ~1 week).
- Approve emergency on-call hours and OPEX to enable manual warmup for other high-value routes this quarter.
- I will brief VP Product and Head of SRE with the write-up.

I'll produce a short post-mortem draft by EOD; Grace to include the estimated credit and Marcus will coordinate messaging with NovaRetail.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
